title: Rank Teams by Votes
summary: Given an array of strings representing votes, sort the teams based on the most first-place votes.
statement: Given an array of strings representing votes, sort the teams based on the most first-place votes. If two or more teams have the same number of first-place votes, resolve the tie by the number of second-place votes, and continue this process for subsequent positions if necessary. If teams are still tied after considering all positions, rank them alphabetically by their team letter. Return the sorted list of teams as a string.
constraints: Every vote ranks the same distinct uppercase teams exactly once.
Compare teams by first-place counts, then second-place counts, continuing through every rank.
If all position counts tie, rank alphabetically.
hints: Count each team separately at every rank position.
Sort by the negated vector of position counts, then by the team letter.
Tuple comparison applies the first differing rank automatically.
This ordering is exactly the rule’s lexicographic sequence of tie breakers.
editorial: Build one count vector per team. Sorting by its negated entries gives descending vote counts at each successive rank; appending the letter gives ascending alphabetical fallback. The oracle independently constructs the same rule with explicit positional counts and a separate tuple key.

tests.explanation: A has five first-place votes; C beats B on second-place votes, producing ACB.
With one vote, return its ranking unchanged.
